responses.content:
There is no credible evidence to suggest that Albert Einstein failed math in school. In fact, most sources agree that Einstein was a diligent and hardworking student, often excelling academically. He attended the Swiss Federal Polytechnic University, where he studied physics and mathematics.

Einstein's academic record at the university is well-documented. According to his own account, he passed all his exams and even received an honorary doctorate from the university in 1921. Additionally, his teacher, Paul Löbisch, wrote that Einstein was "very diligent" and had a strong interest in mathematics.

It's worth noting that Einstein did have some difficulties with math, particularly when it came to advanced calculus and differential equations. However, these challenges were likely due to his own struggles with the subject rather than any failure.
